title: Ljubljana over 20,000 years
episode: 20,000 Years of Ljubljana in 9 Minutes, Built from Real Historical Data
description: A 3D animated map of the Ljubljana basin from the Ice Age to today: lake dwellers in the marshes, Roman Emona, the medieval town below the castle, and the city rebuilt after the earthquake of 1895.

title: The world’s oldest wooden wheel
episode: Ljubljana Marshes Wheel - World's Oldest Wooden Wheel (Slovenia, 5,200 years old)
description: A wheel of ash wood with an oak axle, about 5,200 years old, found in the Ljubljana Marshes south of the city in 2002. It is on display, with the axle, in the city museum.

title: Roman Emona
episode: CtrlArt - Roman Town Historical Reconstruction: Colonia Iulia Emona
description: A digital reconstruction of Emona, the Roman colony laid out on a grid here in the first century AD. A long stretch of its southern wall still stands in Mirje, restored by Plečnik in the 1930s.

title: Plečnik’s “New Athens”
episode: Inside the stunning 'New Athens' of Central Europe - BBC REEL
description: A short BBC film on Jože Plečnik, who spent his last decades remaking Ljubljana as a classical capital for the Slovenes. His National and University Library, finished in 1941, is his masterpiece.

title: The cathedral that was never built
episode: Jože Plečnik's Unrealized "Cathedral of Freedom" Animated For The Very First Time
description: An animation of Plečnik’s design for a Slovene parliament, called the Cathedral of Freedom: a huge cone-shaped building he imagined on the castle hill in 1947. It was never built.

title: How Yugoslavia broke apart
description: An animated history of how Yugoslavia came apart in 1991, beginning with Slovenia, the richest republic, which declared independence on June 25 and fought a short war with the Yugoslav army.

title: The Erased
episode: SLOVENIA | The Tragic Case of Yugoslavia's 'Erased'
description: A political scientist on the Erased: about 25,000 people from other Yugoslav republics who were quietly deleted from Slovenia’s register of residents in 1992. The European Court of Human Rights later ruled against Slovenia.

title: Metelkova
description: How artists and activists occupied the former Yugoslav army barracks at Metelkova in 1993 and turned them into an autonomous cultural center, covered in murals and sculpture, with clubs and galleries.

title: The Slovene language
episode: The Slovenian Language and History [Language Digest]
description: A short introduction to Slovene: its place among the South Slavic languages, its many dialects, and the dual. France Prešeren, the national poet, wrote in Slovene when educated people used German.
